title: ChroDrip - ProteinA/G
author: David Frommholz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vufe6tn
materials: Do you want to purify antibodies or sanitize your column? Please choose below.

steps.title: Load sample onto column
steps.instruction: Add the sample to the top of the column and let it flow through by gravity. Adjust the sample to pH 7.5‑8.5 and 150‑300 mM NaCl; an easy way is to add 1/11 volume of 0.5 M Tris, 2 M NaCl (pH 8.0). Remove particulate matter by centrifugation or 0.45 µm filtration. For slow or weak‑binding antibodies, collect the flow‑through and re‑apply it.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer
steps.instruction: Add 5 column volumes of wash buffer and wait until it has drained. Repeat once more. Keep the flow‑through and wash fractions for later analysis (e.g., SDS‑PAGE). For higher purity repeat the washing step up to 5 times. If needed, include up to 1 % Tween‑20 and/or up to 0.5 M NaCl in the wash buffer.

steps.title: Pre‑elution step
steps.instruction: Add 0.75 column volumes of elution buffer to the column. This fraction does not contain the target protein; it replaces most of the wash buffer and yields a more concentrated eluate.

steps.title: Elute target protein
steps.instruction: Place a clean tube under the column. Add three successive aliquots of 3 column volumes elution buffer, collecting each fraction in a separate tube and waiting for complete drainage between aliquots. For more concentrated eluates, perform 8 successive elutions of 1 column volume each, collecting each fraction separately. Determine which fraction(s) contain most protein and combine them.

steps.title: Prepare column for storage
steps.instruction: Remove the bottom and top caps of the column. If the column is used, first drain the storage solution. Then add 5 column volumes of wash buffer (bed volume is indicated on the column).

steps.title: Clean column after use
steps.instruction: Wash the column successively with 5 column volumes elution buffer, 5 column volumes wash buffer, and 5 column volumes deionized water. Next, add 10 column volumes of 20 % ethanol (or wash buffer containing 0.05 % w/v sodium azide) and wait until half of the buffer has drained. Close the top lid, then the bottom stopper. Store the column at room temperature or 4‑8 °C. For long‑term storage, dry the open column (top and bottom) in an oven at 80 °C for at least 2 hours or overnight, ensure the bottom stopper is completely dry, attach the column outlet, close the lid, and keep the column closed at room temperature.

steps.title: Neutralize eluate
steps.instruction: For each milliliter of eluate, add three drops of neutralization solution.

steps.title: Post‑purification column wash
steps.instruction: After a purification, wash the column with 5 column volumes elution buffer followed by 5 column volumes wash buffer; let the buffer drain. If the column had been stored, let the buffer drain and then wash with an additional 5 column volumes wash buffer.

steps.title: Sanitize column
steps.instruction: Add 5 column volumes sanitization solution, let 1 column volume drain, close the top and bottom caps, and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Drain sanitization and rinse
steps.instruction: Drain the sanitization solution and wash the column with 10 column volumes deionized water.

steps.title: Final storage preparation
steps.instruction: Add approximately 5 column volumes wash buffer (contains 0.05 % w/v sodium azide) and wait until half of the buffer has drained. Close the top lid, then the bottom stopper. Store the column at room temperature or 4‑8 °C and wait at least 12 hours before the next purification. For long‑term storage, dry the open column in an oven at 80 °C for at least 2 hours or overnight, ensure the bottom stopper is dry, attach the outlet, close the lid, and keep the column closed at room temperature.
